# 13. Local SEO

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Support local discovery with accurate business information, useful location content, and compliant structured data.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A canonical NAP record: business name, address or service-area rule, phone, email, hours, and website URL.
- [ ] A Google Business Profile alignment record with exact name, primary category, service categories, service areas, hours, and landing page.
- [ ] A location page template for each real office or service area that has unique local value.
- [ ] LocalBusiness or more specific schema where it accurately represents the visible business.
- [ ] A local proof library including photos, service areas, reviews, case studies, directions, parking, neighborhoods, credentials, and local associations.
- [ ] A citation consistency checklist for major free listings relevant to the business.
- [ ] A review acquisition and response policy that follows platform rules.
- [ ] A map and directions policy that does not require invasive tracking to access essential location information.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Business name, address, phone, hours, and service details must be consistent across site, schema, footer, contact page, and public listings.
- [ ] Location pages must describe real local relevance, not only substitute city names.
- [ ] A service-area business must not publish misleading physical addresses or virtual offices.
- [ ] Local schema must match visible page information and official business facts.
- [ ] The contact page must support local intent with click-to-call, directions, hours, service area, parking or access notes, and response expectations.
- [ ] Reviews must be real, attributed according to permission, and not selectively edited to mislead.
- [ ] Multiple locations must have distinct landing pages with unique NAP and content.
- [ ] Local SEO work must not create doorway pages or duplicate thin pages.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check NAP consistency across footer, contact page, schema, metadata, GBP landing URL, and citations.
- [ ] Check that phone links use tel: format and visible numbers remain readable.
- [ ] Check that hours include holiday or exception handling where relevant.
- [ ] Check that embedded maps have privacy and performance fallbacks.
- [ ] Check that local images are optimized, authentic, and have descriptive alt text.
- [ ] Check that each location page links to relevant services and each service page links to relevant locations.
- [ ] Check that GBP guidelines are followed for eligibility, name, address visibility, categories, and service area behavior.
- [ ] Check that local structured data validates and uses the most specific accurate schema type.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid fake offices, virtual address abuse, keyword-stuffed business names, and misleading service areas.
- [ ] Avoid review gating, fake reviews, copied reviews without permission, and undisclosed incentives.
- [ ] Avoid map embeds that block page load or leak unnecessary data before consent where local law requires consent.
- [ ] Avoid publishing duplicate location pages with only swapped city names.
- [ ] Avoid hiding NAP in images.
- [ ] Avoid inconsistent tracking phone numbers unless call tracking preserves NAP consistency and is documented.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The site must make local trust obvious and verifiable.
- [ ] Location content must help real visitors decide whether the business serves their area.
- [ ] Search engines must receive the same business facts users see.
- [ ] Local visibility work must strengthen reputation rather than exploit listing loopholes.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to detect LocalBusiness schema, phone links, NAP text, location pages, map embeds, and missing image alternatives.
- [ ] Use generated schema templates only with reviewed real business data.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Business name, address, phone, email, service area, location, category, hours, map link, contact page, footer, schema, and public listings are consistent where relevant.
- [ ] Location pages are useful, specific, internally linked, metadata-rich, not thin duplicates, not doorway pages, and include local proof, contact options, and clear CTAs.
- [ ] Local testimonials, local case studies, Google Business Profile, social profiles, directory listings, reviews, opening hours, and service-area language support trust.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
